bibliographic.title: Ethical Considerations in Personal Health Large Language Models
bibliographic.citation_apa: Liu, J., & Liu, S. (2026). Ethical considerations in personal health large language models. Journal of Medical Internet Research, 28, e92240. https://doi.org/10.2196/92240

methodology.study_design: viewpoint article proposing a governance framework
methodology.technology_context: text-based, platform-mediated, dialogue-driven personal health large language models (PH-LLMs) deployed directly to consumers

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a viewpoint focused on text-based, dialogue-driven PH-LLMs in consumer health contexts and proposes a governance framework across privacy, accuracy, equity, transparency, human-AI interaction, and regulatory governance, with implementation mechanisms such as risk-tiered certification, tiered accountability, and postdeployment oversight.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction/abstract text were provided; full-text verification is needed to confirm complete framework content, methods, and limitations.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a conceptual viewpoint rather than an empirical study. The text states the framework is evidence-informed but partly anticipatory; no empirical sample or formal review methodology is described in the provided excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is clearly structured and highly relevant to governed conversational PH-LLMs in regulated health settings, but confidence is moderated because the provided text describes an anticipatory viewpoint without detailed empirical or systematic review methods.

coding.theme: Ethical and regulatory governance of personal health LLMs
coding.subtheme: Operational governance framework for dialogue-driven consumer health LLMs

synthesis.main_claim: Direct-to-consumer, dialogue-driven PH-LLMs create a distinct ethical risk profile that general AI governance frameworks do not fully address, requiring a PH-LLM-specific governance framework.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a governance framework grounded in the four principles of biomedical ethics, operationalized through design and deployment controls and implementation mechanisms including risk-tiered certification, tiered accountability, and postdeployment oversight via adverse-event reporting, transparency reporting, and independent safety evaluation.
synthesis.limitations: The framework is described as evidence-informed but partly anticipatory; full methodological limits are unclear from the provided excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as central conceptual evidence on conversational governance, accountability, safeguards, fairness auditing, and postdeployment oversight for LLM-based personal health systems in regulated healthcare contexts.

evidence.claim: Article type and focus on PH-LLMs
evidence.excerpt: Viewpoint Ethical Considerations in Personal Health Large Language Models
Jialin Liu1,2*, MD; Siru Liu3*, PhD

evidence.claim: PH-LLMs are consumer-facing dialogue systems in health contexts
evidence.excerpt: PH-LLMs are consumer-facing generative systems designed to support individuals through natural language dialogue across health-related contexts

evidence.claim: Focus on text-based dialogue-driven PH-LLMs without clinical oversight
evidence.excerpt: This viewpoint focuses on text-based, dialogue-driven PH-LLMs deployed directly to consumers.

evidence.claim: Distinct governance gap beyond general AI frameworks
evidence.excerpt: Their direct-to-consumer use without clinical oversight creates a distinct ethical risk profile that general artificial intelligence governance frameworks do not fully address.
synthesizes PH-LLM–specific challenges across 6 domains: privacy, accuracy, equity, transparency, human-artificial intelligence interaction, and regulatory governance.

evidence.claim: Framework grounded in biomedical ethics principles
evidence.excerpt: Grounded in the 4 principles of biomedical ethics, we propose a governance framework that operationalizes beneficence, nonmaleficence, autonomy, and justice

through design and deployment controls, including health literacy-aligned communication, crisis and pharmacological safeguards, hallucination mitigation, role disclosure, granular consent, fairness auditing, and accessible design.

evidence.claim: Implementation mechanisms include certification and accountability
evidence.excerpt: implementation mechanisms, including risk-tiered certification, tiered accountability, and postdeployment oversight through adverse-event reporting, transparency reporting, and independent safety evaluation.
This framework is intended as an evidence-informed but partly anticipatory approach to governing PH-LLMs in personal health management.

evidence.claim: Regulated medical device context may apply
evidence.excerpt: Some PH-LLM functions may fall within medical device software regulation when intended for diagnostic, therapeutic, or patient-specific clinical decision support
because they operate on sensitive personal information and may influence high-stakes decisions
We distinguish these systems from general-purpose chatbots by their sustained health-oriented interaction, use of personal health disclosures, and potential to shape real-world health decisions.
